what_it_does: Every processor chip has hardware mechanisms for translating a program's logical view of memory into the actual physical memory locations — a kind of address book managed by the hardware. Writing the operating system code that correctly configures these mechanisms for a specific chip is tedious, repetitive, and error-prone; mistakes can break the isolation between programs and create serious security vulnerabilities. Velosiraptor takes a formal description of what the translation hardware does (its structure and rules) and automatically generates the correct OS code to configure it, rather than having engineers write that code by hand. The generated code is correct by construction, meaning it is mathematically guaranteed to match the hardware's specification, eliminating an entire class of security bugs at the source.
